newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea stocks get $4.45 bln offshore funds in '96.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea stocks get $4.45 bln offshore funds in '96.

text.p: The net inflow of foreign funds to the South Korean stock market last year was $4.45 billion, up from $2.43 billion in 1995, the Bank of Korea said on Wednesday.
Last year $12.41 billion flowed in to stocks from overseas while remittances totalled $7.96 billion, the central bank said in a statement.
In the five years since the Seoul stock market opened to foreign investors in 1992, foreign fund inflows totalled $41.55 billion while remittances amounted to $25 billion, the statement said.
The new foreign inflow thus stood at $16.56 billion by the end of 1996, the central bank said.
In 1996, the net inflow from the United States totalled $2.48 billion, or 55.8 percent of the total, while $378 million came from Britain.
As of the end of November 1996, foreign ownership of local shares totalled 16.305 trillion won, representing 12.83 percent of the Seoul bourse's market capitalisation, the bank said.
The ceiling on foreign stock ownership was raised to an aggregate 20 percent in October from 18 percent, following an expansion by three percentage points in April.
South Korea has pledged to abolish the ceiling from 2000. The cap will be raised by three percentage points annually over the 1997-1999 period.
